description: Push the n=1024/2048 trailing-update GEMMs to FP8 (e4m3) or NVFP4 block-scaled tensor cores (B200 FP8 ~4500 TFLOPS = 2x TF32, NVFP4 ~9000 = 4x), with per-block absmax scaling and a CHEAP FP32 RE-ORTHOGONALIZATION correction to recover accuracy — the operator's specifically-requested lever. The current best routes well-conditioned trailing GEMMs to 1xTF32; FP8/FP4 doubles/quadruples that throughput. The factor budget is loose at n=1024 (~2.4e-3) and n=2048 (~5e-3). A prior attempt found naive FP8 _scaled_mm failed at low batch WITHOUT correction; the new idea is FP8/FP4 GEMM + one FP32 residual-correction pass (recompute the trailing block's high-order error in FP32 and add it back, or a single Newton-Schulz/Gram-Schmidt reorthogonalization of the affected columns). Per-matrix route: well-conditioned -> FP8/FP4+correction, ill -> existing FP32/TF32. Validate AND note remote-portability risk (BF16x9 passed local but failed remote — so any low-precision path must be confirmed remotely later). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

FP8-e4m3 3-term error-compensated trailing GEMM for n=2048 via custom batched mma.sync.m16n8k32 kernel (V^T C and C-=V W on FP8 tensor cores, A_hi*B_hi+A_lo*B_hi+A_hi*B_lo split, per-matrix absmax scaling, stride-aware so it consumes the non-contiguous trailing C view in place). ACCURACY PASSES: all 22 tests + 3 guards clean (n2048 dense factor_scaled=2.2, rankdef=9.6, mixed=2.18, all < 20 gate); the 3-term split recovers ~FP16 (batched trailing relerr ~1.1e-3, single-pass FP8 was ~4e-2 = 16x over gate). SPEED REGRESSES: geomean 11284.666us vs parent 4861.050us (2.3x slower); n2048 shape 30k->122520us. Profile: fp8_bgemm_kernel 52.5%, panel 25.7%, FP8 amax/cast scaling overhead ~10% (reduce 7.2%+elementwise). Root cause: the naive custom FP8 tile kernel (no double-buffer/ldmatrix/async-copy, 1 warp/16 rows, 8 serial n-steps) is ~70x slower than cuBLAS TF32 on these memory-bound thin-cb GEMMs, and 3-term triples MMA work. The trailing GEMM is only ~14-20% of n1024/n2048 time and is memory/launch-bound (BF16 measured SLOWER than TF32 there), so even a perfect FP8 GEMM has a low ceiling here.

Triton 3-term FP8-e4m3 trailing GEMM for n=2048 (replaces the slow custom mma kernel; tl.dot on FP8 -> tuned Blackwell tensor cores). Same 3-term error-compensated split + per-matrix absmax + stride-aware non-contiguous C. ACCURACY PASSES: all 22 tests + 3 guards clean (n2048 factor_scaled 2.25/9.5/2.16 < 20 gate). SPEED: geomean 5147.635us vs parent 4861.050us (5.9% regression, down sharply from trial 1's custom-kernel 2.3x). n2048 shape ~30k(parent TF32)->38364us (~1.3x). Triton FP8 3-term is ~6x faster than the hand mma kernel but still loses to cuBLAS TF32: 3 FP8 GEMMs + amax/cast scaling overhead > one TF32 bmm because the cb=16/32-thin trailing GEMMs are memory/launch-bound, not FLOP-bound. NVFP4 (e2m1) RULED OUT by accuracy: block-scaled 1-term relerr ~1.3e-1, even 3-term ~1.7e-2, both far over gates (1-bit mantissa). Single-pass FP8 (~4e-2) and BF16 (~5.5e-3) also fail the n1024 gate (2.44e-3). Only FP8 3-term meets accuracy, and it costs 3 GEMMs.

Dedupe V/V^T absmax scale in the n=2048 FP8 trailing path (compute sV once, reuse for both GEMMs; the scale reductions were ~11% of n2048 time). All 22 tests + 3 guards PASS. geomean 5128.159us vs parent 4861.050us (~5.5% regression, marginally better than trial 2's 5147.635). n2048 ~36659us clean (one 79557us read was GPU-contention noise; re-measure confirmed -- noise can be ~2x, must re-measure deltas). Trial-2 profile breakdown at n2048: panel 39.4%, Triton FP8 GEMM 27.2%, FP8 scale/cast bookkeeping ~31% (amax-reduce 11% + abs/clamp/elementwise ~18% + W1-zeros). The cast/scale overhead now rivals the GEMM and is the key remaining inefficiency; fusing absmax+cast into the kernel or emitting V's scale from the panel kernel would cut it. STILL a regression because the trailing GEMM is memory-bound and FP8 needs 3 terms for accuracy.

FP8 3-term for the n=1024 well-conditioned trailing (the brief's PRIMARY target). The 22 fixed test shapes PASS but n=1024 ill cases sit at the gate edge (rankdef factor_scaled=18.2, nearrank=19.1, clustered=14.9 vs the 20 gate). DIFFERENTIAL-CORRECTNESS GUARD FAILS: n=1024 nearrank benchmark shape gives a wrong factorization on 3 of 8 distinct seeds. Root cause: _classify_well keys on row-range/density, so nearrank (ill-conditioned but DENSE) is labeled WELL and routed to FP8; the 3-term FP8 error (~1.1e-3/GEMM) compounds over 32 panels at n=1024 and tips over the gate on some seeds. So FP8 at n=1024 is on the accuracy knife-edge for ill-but-dense inputs and is NOT seed-robust. Resetting to trial 3 (n=2048-only FP8, which passes all guards). Open: a 4-term split or a tighter classifier (route nearrank/rankdef to FP32) could make n=1024 FP8 safe, but both add cost on a lever that already regresses speed.

beta=0 fast path for the W1 FP8 GEMM (skip zeros-fill + prev-read on V^T C). All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. geomean ~5120-5133us (two clean runs) vs parent 4861.050us (~5.4% regression); n2048 ~36000us. Marginal vs trial 3 -- W1 zeros were small. Trial-5 n2048 profile: FP8 GEMM 35.7%, panel 35.6%, scaling/cast overhead ~26% (elementwise 15.7% + amax-reduce 8.5%, reduce count dropped 1016->762 from the dedupe). The ~5% regression is fundamental: n2048 trailing is ~20% of the shape, FP8 needs 3 terms for accuracy, and absmax reductions add memory passes on an already memory-bound GEMM. OPEN directions not yet built: (1) fuse absmax+cast into one kernel or emit V's scale from the panel kernel to cut the ~26% overhead; (2) a tighter classifier (route nearrank/rankdef to FP32) to make n=1024 FP8 seed-safe (trial 4 failed the diff guard at the gate edge); (3) 4-term FP8 for n=1024 margin (more cost). None likely to turn a NET win given the memory-bound trailing.

Built and measured the FP8/NVFP4 + correction trailing-GEMM lever exhaustively; 5 trials (4 succeeded, 1 validation_error). Branch HEAD = trial 5 (3db5857db): FP8-e4m3 3-term error-compensated trailing GEMMs for n=2048, all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN, geomean 5120us vs parent 4861us (~5.4% REGRESSION). The brief's lever does not beat TF32 on these shapes -- a real measured negative, with the root cause pinned.

KEY MEASUREMENTS:
- Trailing GEMM is only ~14% of n1024 / ~20% of n2048 time (panel dominates: 83.5%/77.5%). Small lever ceiling (~2.6% geomean even if free).
- The trailing GEMMs are MEMORY/LAUNCH-bound (cb=16/32 thin), not FLOP-bound: BF16 bmm measured SLOWER than TF32 here, so low-precision throughput cannot help and the cast/scale ADDS traffic.
- ACCURACY: single-pass FP8 ~4e-2 and BF16 ~5.5e-3 both FAIL the n1024 gate (2.44e-3); only the 3-term FP8 split (A_hi*B_hi+A_lo*B_hi+A_hi*B_lo) reaches ~1.1e-3. NVFP4/e2m1 RULED OUT: block-scaled 1-term ~1.3e-1, 3-term ~1.7e-2 (1-bit mantissa too coarse).
- BATCHED FP8 PATHS: torch._scaled_grouped_mm (3D) is BROKEN on this build (cudaErrorLaunchFailure even on tiny aligned shapes); torch._scaled_mm is 2D-only and the per-matrix python loop is 25-87x slower than TF32; torch.bmm has no FP8 (baddbmm_cuda unimplemented). So a custom batched FP8 GEMM is required.
- Custom mma.sync.m16n8k32.e4m3 kernel: correct + 3-term accurate but ~70x slower than cuBLAS TF32 (naive tiling). Triton tl.dot FP8: ~6x faster than the hand kernel but still ~1.3x the TF32 cost on these shapes (3 GEMMs + scaling).
- n=1024 FP8 (the PRIMARY target, trial 4): the 22 fixed tests PASS but at the gate edge (rankdef 18.2, nearrank 19.1 vs 20); the DIFF-CORRECTNESS guard FAILS (n1024 nearrank wrong on 3/8 seeds) because the classifier routes ill-but-dense nearrank to FP8. FP8 is NOT seed-safe at n=1024.
- n=2048 FP8 overhead profile: GEMM ~36%, panel ~36%, FP8 scale/cast bookkeeping ~26% (amax-reduce + cast over the large non-contiguous C). I cut it via V/V^T scale dedupe (trial 3) and W1 beta=0 (trial 5); marginal.

OPEN directions I did NOT fully build (manager to steer):
1. Fuse absmax+cast into one kernel, or EMIT V's per-matrix absmax from the panel kernel (it already has V in SMEM) and derive sW analytically -- could cut the ~26% overhead toward n2048 PARITY (not a clear win, since GEMM-only would ~match TF32).
2. Make n=1024 FP8 seed-safe: tighten _classify_well to route nearrank/rankdef (ill-but-dense) to FP32, or use a 4-term FP8 split for margin (more cost) -- then re-measure n=1024 (3 of 12 benchmark shapes).
3. Pre-quantize C to fp8 once (1/4 bytes) so the 3-term GEMM reads fp8 instead of fp32+inline-cast -- cuts the memory-bound GEMM's traffic.
4. cuBLASLt FP8 strided-batched via a C++ extension (the proper library path) -- NOT attempted: no local cublasLt header, torch bundles no static cublas, and the memory note flags low-precision custom ops as remote-portability-risky (BF16x9 failed remote on qr_v2). Needs remote confirmation if pursued.
REMOTE-PORTABILITY NOTE: this FP8 path builds against stock CUDA 13 / torch-bundled Triton only (no extra libs), but per the qr_v2 BF16x9 precedent any low-precision path MUST be confirmed on the remote leaderboard before trust.
